title: Response body size is capped both on Content-Length and on actual bytes read
description: In fetch_session(), call(), and download_blob(), the size limit is enforced twice: once on the Content-Length header and once on the actual bytes returned by resp.bytes(). The code comment explains why: 'Content-Length can lie'. A contributor might remove the second check as redundant. But a malicious or buggy server can send a small Content-Length header and then stream arbitrarily many bytes. The Content-Length check is an optimization (early exit before buffering); the actual-read check is the enforcement guarantee. Both are required. Do not remove either check.
